case.label: C
case.text: Copying open orders into a second table with a stream-triggered Lambda function also stops the nightly Scan from reading the whole main table, so it too cuts the read capacity the report job takes from the main table, and the stream read does not use table read capacity. It loses to B only on cost (extra table, extra writes, Lambda invocations, more moving parts), and the stem's 'MOST cost-effective' wording is what separates them. Option E is a weaker case: strongly consistent reads are not served from the DAX cache but passed through to DynamoDB.

case.label: A
case.text: One new item per vote with a unique key spreads writes across partitions and removes the single hot item, so it also stops the throttling. It loses because the per-second total is then a Scan of the whole table with a filter, which reads every vote item and is slow and costly, while the stem says the total is read every second. B and D fail on the per-partition limit for a single item, which neither on-demand mode nor a higher table-level setting lifts.

case.label: D
case.text: Splitting each recording into chunk items under the call ID technically works and keeps everything in DynamoDB, so a candidate who ignores cost could defend it. It needs many writes and reads at DynamoDB prices for rarely opened multi-MB data and extra application logic, so it is not the most cost-effective option. C fails because a single item has a size limit far below several MB, and A is an in-memory cache, not a durable store.

case.label: B
case.text: A TransactWriteItems call with one Put action and a condition on a version attribute would also reject the stale save, so it detects the conflict. It is the weaker answer because transactional writes use double the write capacity of a standard write for no gain with a single item, and the option does not say the version is added or increased. Only the 'MOST cost-effective' wording separates B from C. A fails because a read before the write still leaves a race window, and D fails because BatchWriteItem is not atomic and supports no conditions.
